text.en: Ravi measures the desk with his hand span and gets 7. Meena gets 6. Same desk, different answers! To avoid this we need standard units.

Measurement gives numbers so everyone can agree. Long ago people used a hand span or a foot, but those differ from person to person. So we use standard units, the same for everyone.
The standard unit of length in the SI system is the metre. Smaller lengths use the centimetre and millimetre. Long distances use the kilometre. 1 metre equals 100 centimetres. 1 centimetre equals 10 millimetres. 1 kilometre equals 1000 metres.
Place the ruler along the object with zero at one end. Look straight down at the mark to avoid parallax error. If the end of the ruler is worn, start from a clear mark like 1 cm and subtract. To measure a curved line, lay a thread along it, straighten the thread and measure the thread.
An object is in motion when its position changes with time compared with a fixed point, called a reference point. A person sitting in a moving bus is at rest for the seat but moving for the road.
Straight line motion is movement along a line, such as a car on a straight road. Circular motion is movement around a fixed point, such as a point on a fan blade. Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals, like a swing or a pendulum. Rotational motion is spinning about an axis, like a top.
